<!-- pr-reviewer: f5d8c06acfa8b7acb429a10b19042a81fa4cd571 -->
**Verdict: Ready for the maintainer to merge** (after parent #551, which was reviewed clean at b262e79f; this review covers only what #560 adds: `pull/551/head...pull/560/head`, 4 files, +295/-2).

**What looks good**
- Additive: `edm.conditions` is `Vec` with `skip_serializing_if = "Vec::is_empty"` and parse returns an empty list when absent, so old files and the template load and save unchanged.
- Load refuses by name (`crates/post/src/machine/edm.rs` parse_conditions): missing or blank id, duplicate id, non-word strings, non-numeric values, negative values, zero wire diameter, unknown role. `is_sane` (`condition_ok`, `unique_ids`) restates the law for project files, so a hand-edited project cannot slip a NaN gap or duplicate id through. Lengths scale with the file's unit.
- `Edm::condition(machine, id, need)` refuses a missing condition or unstated needed field by machine, id and field name. No defaulting anywhere; absent stays `None`, never 0.
- No unwrap/expect/panic in the new code. `edm.rs` is 328 lines. Provenance lines present (module and test header). Decision file `docs/decisions/531-edm-conditions.md` present. Body has `Changelog:` and `Fixes #531`. No data shipped (D4), tests use a synthetic table.
- No process files, build.rs, scripts, dependencies, golden or snapshot changes.

**Local results (merged with current upstream/main, clean auto-merge)**
| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| camcraft-post (all targets) | pass (16, 3, 9, 3, 2, 33 across binaries) |
| app edm_conditions | 6/6 |
| app edm_machine | 7/7 |
| app machine | 33/33 |
| app machine_library | 11/11 |
| app posting | 17/17 |
| clippy -p camcraft-post -p camcraft-app --all-targets -D warnings | clean |

**Requested before merge**: none.

**Notes for #532 / #541 (not blocking)**
1. The lookup is by `id` only. There is no selection by material, wire/electrode or pass: `role` (rough/skim/finish) is stored but nothing looks it up, and `wire_diameter`/`undersize` are per-condition values, not keys. The id is the control's selector, so an op names the id explicitly. #532 must decide whether a pass list names ids (likely, one id per pass) or wants a `by_role` helper; if so, it should refuse by name when zero or several conditions match a role rather than pick the first.
2. `ConditionField` is a closed enum (Gap, WireDiameter, Undersize). A wire op needs `[Gap, WireDiameter]`, a sinker op `[Gap, Undersize]` (#541). A condition may state both wire and undersize fields; nothing rejects a sinker field on a wire machine. Fine as is, but the op command is the place to enforce kind.
3. There is no cross-check between `condition.wire_diameter` and the machine's `wire_diameters` list. #532 should decide whether a condition's wire must be in that list, and refuse by name if so.
4. A numeric id uses `n.to_string()`, so `1.0` reads as "1.0" rather than "1". Harmless but worth a test if controls use numeric selectors.
5. The shape (flat table, additive, id-keyed, `Result<&Condition, String>`) looks stable; adding keys later is low cost.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.

<!-- pr-reviewer: 65588c59b3357fef84bd0f078f9b5085742b7a89 -->
**Ready for the maintainer to merge** (after #551). All 8 items from the review at f5d8c06a are verified point by point at 65588c59.

Reviewed what #560 adds over #551. Merge 88814094 only moves the table into `crates/post/src/machine/edm_conditions.rs`; the fixes are in 65588c59. Trial merge with current upstream/main: "Already up to date" (the branch already carries main). No build.rs, `.github`, script, dependency or PNG change.

### The 8 requested items
1. **Bounded geometry** - met. `condition_refusal` (`edm_conditions.rs`): `gap` must be finite and > 0; `gap >= wire_diameter/2` refuses when both are stated; `wire_diameter` and `undersize` must lie in (0, 1] mm (`MAX_WIRE_MM`) after scaling. Every refusal is wrapped by the reader as `edm condition "<id>" <key>: <value> mm ...`, so it names the id, key and unit. `conditions_sane` (via `Edm::is_sane`) calls the same function, so the project door has the same law. Pinned by `the_kerf_geometry_is_bounded_by_name` and `a_hand_edited_project_machine_with_a_bad_table_is_not_sane`.
2. **Kind-specific fields** - met. `parse_conditions` takes the declared `Kind`; `undersize` on a wire gives `edm condition "C1" undersize is a sinker field; this is a wire_edm machine`, and `wire_diameter` on a sinker is the mirror. A stored table is also covered by `Edm::fits`. Pinned by `a_condition_states_only_its_kinds_field`.
3. **Wire in the machine's list** - met. When `edm.wire_diameters` is stated, a condition wire must be within 0.001 mm of one of them (both sides in mm after scaling; the list is parsed before the conditions). When none is stated, any wire in range passes, and that is documented. Tolerance judgement: 0.001 mm is 1 micron, well below any real wire step (0.02-0.5 mm wires differ by at least ~0.01 mm) and above float noise from an inch conversion (0.01 in vs 0.254 mm). Good. Pinned by `a_conditions_wire_must_be_one_the_machine_takes`.
4. **One selector, one id** - met. Surrounding spaces refuse (not trimmed); a numeric id must be a whole number >= 0 (`1.0`, `1.5`, `-3` refuse); duplicates refuse by `id_key` (case-insensitive, leading zeros ignored), so `C1`/`c1` and `01`/`1` refuse as a pair. The lookup is exact, as the decision file says. Judgement: with the uniqueness rule, exact lookup cannot be made ambiguous: any selector the user writes can equal at most one stored id, and no other row can collide with it under the case/zero key. Residual (not blocking): ids that differ only by internal whitespace (`C 1` vs `C1`) or non-ASCII look-alikes stay distinct words; that is the correct reading since the id is posted to the control as written. Pinned by `one_selector_answers_one_condition`.
5. **Unknown keys** - met. `edm condition "C1" gapp is not a condition key (id, name, gap, ...)`. Pinned by `an_unknown_condition_key_is_refused_by_name`.
6. **Finite after scaling** - met. `num` scales then checks `is_finite`; an inch file with `1e308` refuses naming the id and key. Pinned by `a_condition_length_that_overflows_once_scaled_is_refused_by_name`.
7. **Documented** - met. `assets/machines/AGENTS.md` has the key table with units, bounds, the id rule, the wire-list rule (stated vs not stated), the kind-only fields, and "absent and `[]` read the same: no table, every EDM op refuses", plus `is_sane` for hand-edited projects. The decision file `docs/decisions/531-edm-conditions.md` records the same.
8. **Cohesion** - met. Parser tests are in `crates/post/src/machine/edm_conditions_tests.rs` (11 tests); only `the_table_rides_the_project_file` stays in `crates/app/tests/edm_conditions.rs`. Count went from 6 to 12, not reduced. `edm.rs` is 302 lines, `edm_conditions.rs` 272.

### Local results (worktree's own target/, sccache)
| Suite | Result |
|---|---|
| `cargo test -p camcraft-post` (lib 35, axis_direction_cli 3, comp 9, comp_plane 3, cycle_hop 7, mch_head_search 2, post_engine 33, recorded_streams 10, script_* 9 each) | pass |
| app `edm_conditions` 1, `edm_machine` 5, `machine` 33, `machine_library` 11, `posting` 17 | pass |
| `cargo clippy -p camcraft-post -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings` | clean |

(`edm_machine` is 5 here against 7 in the earlier review: the parser cases moved to camcraft-post in #551's ebf0644b, not in this PR.)

### Notes (not blocking)
- A comment on this PR says a trial merge into #1156's branch conflicts in `crates/app/src/mcp/mod.rs` and `crates/ui/src/egui_app/panes.rs` (keep both sides); that is for the #1156 author, not this PR.
- The kerf consumer (#1123) is reviewed separately; these bounds are what it will trust.

Merge order: #551 first, then this. Both are `feat` and merge at the next cut.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.

<!-- pr-reviewer: d03e58e2da41df98332ccc516cd8a7d446acb2ae -->
**Ready for the maintainer to merge.** Both requests left from our review of `65588c59` are fixed, and they hold under probe. The delta adds no new blockers.

This is a delta re-check of `65588c59..d03e58e2`: the merge of main `a802866a`, then the fix `d03e58e2`. Trial-merged locally with main `3aa8f3ef` (after #1191): clean, never pushed. `git show --remerge-diff a802866a` is empty, so the merge carries no hand edits. The fix touches three files: `crates/post/src/machine/edm_conditions.rs`, its tests, and `assets/machines/AGENTS.md`. It adds no dependencies and touches no build.rs, scripts, `.github/` or process files.

### Requests from the review of 65588c59
| # | Request | Status | Probe at d03e58e2 (merged with main) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Lower bound on `wire_diameter` | **fixed** | `MIN_WIRE_MM = 0.02`. mm `0.010` -> `edm condition "C1" wire_diameter: 0.01 mm is outside [0.02, 1] mm`. `0.02` and `1` pass exactly at the bounds; `0.0199999`, `1.0000001` and `-0.25` refuse. |
| 2 | `gap` bounded on its own; sinker `gap > undersize` refused | **fixed** | `MAX_GAP_MM = 0.5`. `{ "id": "C1", "gap": 5 }` (no wire) -> `gap: 5 mm is outside (0, 0.5] mm`. `0.5` passes; `0.5000001` and sinker `0.6` refuse. Sinker gap `0.1000001` / undersize `0.1` -> `gap: 0.1000001 mm is larger than the undersize (0.1 mm) - ...`. `0.5`/`0.5` passes. |

**Units.** The bounds apply after scaling to mm, as AGENTS.md says:
- An inch file's `0.010` in wire (0.254 mm) passes.
- An inch `0.0008` in wire (0.02032 mm) passes; `0.00078` in (0.019812 mm) refuses.
- An inch gap of `0.02` in (0.508 mm) refuses; `0.0196` in (0.498 mm) passes.
- On an inch sinker, gap `0.004` with undersize `0.004` passes (both scale the same way). Gap `0.005` with undersize `0.004` refuses as `0.127 mm ... (0.1016 mm)`.
- An inch gap of `1e307` is still refused by the earlier finite-after-scaling rule.

**NaN, infinities and negative values.** These are checked at the project gate (`Machine::is_sane` on a hand-built `Condition`, since JSON cannot carry NaN):
- A gap or undersize of NaN or ±inf -> not sane.
- A wire of NaN or -inf -> not sane; a wire of 0.019 -> not sane; a wire of 0.02 -> sane.
- A negative gap, wire or undersize is refused by name.

**Order of the checks.** The wire-radius rule still runs before the new gap bound, so its message is unchanged. With a wire stated, `gap < d/2 <= 0.5` already holds, so `MAX_GAP_MM` only fires when no wire is stated.

**Every refusal names its condition.** Each one carries the id, the key, the value and `mm` (with an `edm condition "<id>"` prefix from the reader).

**Lookup unchanged.** The stack above (#1131, #1136, #1156, #1123) depends on `Edm::condition`. The commit does not touch it: `Edm::condition(&self, machine: &str, id: &str, need: &[ConditionField]) -> Result<&Condition, String>` is unchanged, as are its exact-match `find(|c| c.id == id)` and its error text.

### What looks good
- Each bound is a named constant taken from the range the provenance comment already cites, and the docs state the same numbers.
- The pins cover each new refusal and each edge that must pass, including the inch 0.010 in.
- `a_hand_edited_project_machine_with_a_bad_table_is_not_sane` covers the sinker rule at the project door too, so both doors share one law.
- `edm_conditions.rs` is 298 lines, under the 400-line cap. It has no `unwrap()`, `expect(` or `panic!`.

### Local results (merged with main 3aa8f3ef, Windows, debug)
- `cargo test -p camcraft-post`: all pass. lib 38 (it was 35; the new pins are in the existing fns), post_engine 33, recorded_streams 12, cycle_hop 7, comp 9, comp_plane 3, axis_direction_cli 3, mch_head_search 2, vendor_mch_cli 2, script_* 11 each, script_fanuc_lathe 15.
- `cargo test -p camcraft-app`: all pass. edm_conditions 1, edm_machine 5, machine 33, machine_edit 12, machine_key_order 2, machine_library 11, plasma_machine 6, posting 17, project_roundtrip 71.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-post -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- I also ran a throwaway probe test locally for the boundary, unit and NaN cases above. It was removed afterwards and never pushed.

### Requested before merge
None.

### Questions / notes (not blocking)
1. **Gap equal to the undersize passes. I think that is the right reading.** In die-sinking, a finishing electrode's undersize per side is sized to the finishing condition's overcut (spark gap), so the cavity burns to the nominal wall. Refusing equality would refuse the textbook finishing electrode. Practical sizing often adds a little for the surface-roughness depth, so `undersize >= gap` is the minimum. `undersize < gap` is the case that burns past the wall, and that is the one refused. A rough condition with `gap == undersize` leaves no finish stock, but it still does not cut past the wall. One limit: the rule compares fields inside one condition only. An op that runs a roughing condition (large gap) with an electrode undersized for the finish has to check that pairing itself. That belongs to the sinker op (#1136), not to this table.
2. Refusals in an inch file print the scaled mm value (`0.019812 mm`), not what the user typed (`0.00078` in). The unit is named correctly. Echoing the value as written as well would help a user find the line. This pattern was there before the fix.
3. A negative gap reads `gap: -0.1 mm must be above 0 mm (a spark gap of zero cannot be meant)`. The aside fits a zero gap, not a negative one. A finite huge mm gap (`1e308`) prints all its digits. Both are cosmetic and were there before the fix.
4. Carried over from the last review: please add a line to `assets/machines/AGENTS.md` saying `"C01"` and `"C1"` are two ids (leading zeros count only in an all-digit id).
5. As the fix's own comment says, #1123 (`issue/532-wire-contour`) will need this branch's `edm_conditions.rs` and message texts when it merges. Its `S9` (an undersize on a wire) is refused by the kind rule.

Merge order: this PR is first in the chain (#560 -> #1131 -> #1136 -> #1156).

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
